evidence: app/src/pages/abilities/[name].astro:1 — self-contained route; delete the file and the feature's pages are gone
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:106 — the only other file touched: one Section block and the abilities const at :45
app/src/layouts/Layout.astro:20-23 — nav hardcodes only Pokémon/Types, so no nav edit is needed
app/src/styles/global.css:276 — .card__note is used only by the ability page (minor dead CSS if left)
removability.rationale: Deleting the abilities feature is a two-file change with no entanglement elsewhere; the only residue is two tiny CSS rules, and touching the Pokémon page is inherent to the spec, not a design flaw.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:73 — spriteUrl is the single sprite source for every card list, so a sprite fix lands in one place
app/src/lib/api.ts:92-103 — pokemonRefsToSpecies centrally resolves Pokémon refs to species (the Deoxys case), shared by moves/abilities/types pages
app/src/pages/moves/[name].astro:25 — effect fallback chain (short_effect ?? flavor ?? '—') duplicated verbatim at pages/abilities/[name].astro:17
app/src/pages/index.astro:126-133 — fetch/DOMParser/abort-then-swap client logic duplicated at components/MoveTables.astro:117-133
app/src/pages/types/[name].astro:26-30 — page maps raw API fields inline with `any` casts, so API-shape changes are found page-by-page
changeability.rationale: The two most likely bugs (sprites, species-vs-Pokémon references) have single fix points, but the effect fallback chain and the client-side fetch-and-swap helper each exist twice, so those fixes must be applied in N places.

evidence: app/src/components/PokemonCard.astro:6-12 — narrow, optional-prop interface (id, name, types, note); pages never reach into its internals
app/src/lib/moves.ts:19-20 — getMoveTables returns typed data; MoveTables.astro is a dumb renderer over that seam
app/src/components/MoveTables.astro:117-133 — client script only manipulates rendered markup; all data comes from server-rendered partials, a clean server/client split
app/src/components/MoveTables.astro:37-38 — takes pokemonName solely to build the form action URL, coupling a generic table component to the Pokémon route
app/src/components/TypeBadge.astro:14 — `var(--type-<name>)` fallback string duplicated at pages/types/index.astro:15, so the styling convention leaks outside the component
coupling.rationale: Components depend on narrow typed props and the data layer is a clean seam, but some API-shape knowledge lives inline in pages with `any` casts, and MoveTables knows the Pokémon route for its form action.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:92-103 — pokemonRefsToSpecies is a genuine abstraction: one helper covers the Pokémon-referenced-by-resource case for three pages, dedupes and excludes alternate forms
app/src/components/MoveTables.astro:20-27 — the level-up-only Level column is handled by composition, not a boolean flag on the component
app/src/components/Section.astro:1-15 — section-with-heading landmark pattern extracted once and reused on every page
app/src/pages/types/index.astro:15 — duplicates TypeBadge's badge styling inline instead of reusing the component, a small copy-paste seam
app/src/lib/api.ts:151-171 — getPokemonIndex returns a page-shaped grab bag (entries + types + generations) tailored to one route; an Items-style reuse would re-derive parts of it
abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions track the app's real variation (refs→species, per-method move tables, sections) and stretch without flag creep; a shared resource-page scaffold is the one missing abstraction, leaving a little copy-paste across detail pages.

findings.issue: The effect fallback chain (englishShortEffect ?? latestEnglishFlavorText ?? '—') is duplicated verbatim in abilities/[name].astro:17, so changing the fallback rules means editing both pages.
findings.suggestion: Add an `englishEffect(resource)` helper to src/lib/api.ts that owns the chain, and call it from both pages.

findings.issue: The fetch + DOMParser + AbortController partial-swap client logic (~18 lines) is duplicated in components/MoveTables.astro:124-131; a bug in abort/error handling or a switch to Astro actions would be fixed twice.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared client util (e.g. src/lib/swap.ts exporting `swapRegion(url, selector)`) and import it from both scripts.

findings.issue: Pages map raw API records inline with `any` casts (also types/[name].astro:26-30, index.astro:15-20), so a change in API payload shape must be hunted across page frontmatter.
findings.suggestion: Move per-resource mapping (abilities, types, stats, moves list) into typed helpers in src/lib/ so pages consume app-shaped data.

findings.issue: The `var(--type-<name>, var(--color-text-muted))` inline-style convention is duplicated from TypeBadge.astro:14,18; changing the fallback color or badge styling takes two edits.
findings.suggestion: Render the type list with a variant of the TypeBadge component (or a shared CSS class) so the convention lives in one place.

findings.issue: getPokemonIndex returns a bundle shaped for the home page (entries, types, generations); a second consumer or a home-page redesign churns its return type.
findings.suggestion: Split into narrow exports (species index, types, generations) and let the page compose them.

findings.issue: Feature-specific rules (.card__note used only by abilities, .game-picker only by MoveTables) live in one global file, so removing a feature can leave dead CSS.
findings.suggestion: Use Astro scoped <style> blocks in the owning components (PokemonCard.astro, MoveTables.astro) for feature-specific styles.

summary: This is a well-factored Astro 7 app: data access, species/reference resolution and sprite URLs each have a single home in src/lib/api.ts, all four card lists share one component, and the page scaffolding (Layout, Section, NotFound) is reused rather than duplicated. The scenarios mostly land in one or two files, including the plausible Deoxys sprite bug, which has an obvious single fix point. What keeps it from exemplary is a pair of verbatim duplications (the effect fallback chain, the client-side fetch-and-swap code) and API-shape knowledge scattered into page frontmatter with `any` casts.
